meta.titre: Vocabulary in Context: working out meaning from clues
meta.sous_theme: Finding the meaning of words and expressions from their context
tags: O Level English - vocabulary in context

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L English Language past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A cloth seller in Douala hears a customer say, "That price is steep," and sees her put the cloth back on the pile. The seller does not need a dictionary: the customer's face and her action show that "steep" means "too high" here. Questions on vocabulary in Paper 1 work in the same way. They ask what a word or an expression means in this sentence or this passage, not what a dictionary lists first. If you learn to read the clues around a word, you can answer such questions even when the word is new to you.

items: A synonym is a word with nearly the same meaning as another word, and an antonym has the opposite meaning.
Nouns name things, verbs show actions, adjectives describe nouns and adverbs describe verbs.
An idiom is a fixed expression whose meaning is different from the meanings of its separate words.

sections.titre: Reading the clues around a word
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Meaning comes from the sentence

Most English words have more than one meaning. The word *bank* can be the side of a river or a place that keeps money. The sentence around the word shows which meaning is used. Vocabulary questions therefore test how well you read clues, not how many words you have memorised.

### Five kinds of clue

| Clue | What the writer does | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Definition | Explains the word | *The farmer was frugal, which means that he spent money very carefully.* |
| Restatement | Repeats the idea in other words | *The soldier was courageous, brave in every battle he fought.* |
| Contrast | Gives the opposite idea | *Unlike his talkative brother, Ayuk was taciturn.* (taciturn = saying very little) |
| Example | Lists examples of the word | *She loves citrus fruits, such as oranges and lemons.* |
| Cause and effect | Shows a reason or a result | *Because the harvest was meagre, many families went hungry.* (meagre = small in amount) |

### The substitution test

Put each option in the place of the word. The sentence must still make sense and must stay grammatical. If the tested word is an adjective, the answer must also work as an adjective.

### Meanings of word parts

| Part | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| un-, dis-, in-, im- | not, the opposite | unkind, dislike, incorrect, impolite |
| re- | again | rewrite |
| pre- | before | pre-school |
| -less | without | careless |
| -ful | full of | careful |

### In the listening part

Some questions ask about a word taken from the passage that was read to you. Recall the sentence in which you heard the word and use the same clues.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When one word is quoted or underlined
variantes.contenu_markdown: Name the part of speech, find the clue in the sentence, predict a meaning before you look at the options, then check each option with the substitution test. Choose the one that fits this sentence, even if you know another meaning of the word.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a group of words is tested
variantes.contenu_markdown: Do not translate word by word. Think about the situation in which the expression is used. *Cost an arm and a leg* means to be very expensive. *Under the weather* means slightly ill. *A blessing in disguise* means something that seems bad but turns out to be good.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the stem asks which word or phrase has the same meaning as a given word
variantes.contenu_markdown: Choose the option that can replace the word in the sentence without changing the meaning. Synonyms are rarely identical: *angry* and *furious* are close, but *furious* is stronger. Pick the one closest in strength and tone to the original word.

sections.enonce_markdown:
In the sentence "Although the teacher's instructions were clear, the pupils' replies were vague," the word "vague" means ______.
A) loud   B) unclear   C) polite   D) correct

etapes.action: Identify the word and its part of speech.
etapes.justification: 'Vague' describes the noun 'replies', so it is an adjective. The answer must also be an adjective.

etapes.action: Find the clue in the sentence.
etapes.justification: The word 'Although' signals a contrast. The instructions were clear, so the replies must have been the opposite of clear.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Contrast clue: 'Although ... clear' points to 'not clear'.

etapes.action: Predict the meaning before reading the options.
etapes.justification: A prediction stops the options from pulling you towards a wrong idea.
Loud replies, polite replies and correct replies do not contrast with clear instructions in a logical way, whereas 'unclear replies' does.
etapes.resultat_markdown: A) not a contrast; B) fits; C) not a contrast; D) 'correct' does not contrast with 'clear'.

etapes.action: Choose the option and re-read the full sentence.
etapes.justification: Reading the sentence with the chosen word confirms that it is logical.
etapes.resultat_markdown: 'Although the teacher's instructions were clear, the pupils' replies were unclear.' Answer **B**.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The answer is **B) unclear**. The contrast word *Although* shows that the replies were not clear, and the substitution test confirms that only *unclear* keeps the sentence logical.

items.erreur_markdown: A student reads "They fished from the bank of the river" and chooses "a place where money is kept".
items.pourquoi_faux: The student used the most familiar meaning of the word and ignored the sentence. Fishing and a river show that *bank* means the land at the edge of the water.
items.correction_markdown: Use the clue words (fished, river): *bank* = the side of the river.

items.erreur_markdown: The sentence is "She was feeling under the weather, so she stayed in bed." A student chooses "standing in the rain".
items.pourquoi_faux: The student took the idiom word by word. An idiom has its own meaning.
items.correction_markdown: *Under the weather* means slightly ill. The clue 'stayed in bed' supports this.

items.erreur_markdown: For "The frail old man leaned on a stick", a student chooses the option "weakness".
items.pourquoi_faux: 'Weakness' is a noun. The substitution fails: 'the weakness old man' is not grammatical. The answer must be an adjective.
items.correction_markdown: *Frail* = weak and delicate. The correct option must be an adjective such as 'weak'.

items.erreur_markdown: A student chooses "correct" as the meaning of *inaccurate*.
items.pourquoi_faux: The prefix *in-* means 'not'. The student ignored the prefix and read the word as *accurate*.

items.erreur_markdown: For "The sprinter was exhausted after the race", a student chooses "fast" because the sentence is about running.
items.pourquoi_faux: The option fits the topic but not the meaning of the word. The clue 'after the race' points to tiredness.
items.correction_markdown: *Exhausted* = extremely tired. Choose the option that means this.

items.enonce_markdown:
Choose the word closest in meaning to "enormous".
A) very small   B) very large   C) very old   D) very quiet
items.solution_markdown: "Enormous" means extremely big, so the answer is **B**. The other options describe size, age and sound, which have nothing to do with the word.

items.enonce_markdown:
In the sentence "The nurse's gentle words had a soothing effect on the frightened child, who stopped crying and fell asleep," the word "soothing" means ______.
A) noisy   B) painful   C) calming   D) surprising
items.solution_markdown: The result clue is that the child "stopped crying and fell asleep", so the words made the child calm. Substitution: 'a calming effect on the frightened child' makes sense. Answer: **C**. 'Noisy' and 'painful' are opposites of what happened, and 'surprising' does not explain why the child fell asleep.

items.enonce_markdown:
(a) The thief ran out of sight, but the police were hot on his heels. The expression "hot on his heels" means ______.
A) burning his feet   B) giving up the chase   C) following him very closely   D) running ahead of him

(b) Which sentence uses "bank" with the same meaning as in "They fished from the bank of the river"?
A) The bank manager gave her a loan.   B) Tall grass grew along the bank of the stream.   C) He wants to bank his savings today.   D) The bank closes at four.

(c) The unreliable bus often arrived an hour late. The word "unreliable" means ______.
A) easy to read   B) very fast   C) recently repaired   D) that cannot be depended on
items.solution_markdown:
(a) The thief is running away and the police are chasing him, so "hot on his heels" means following very closely. Answer: **C**. It is an idiom, so the words are not taken literally.

(b) In the model sentence, *bank* is the land beside water. Only sentence B talks about land beside a stream (grass along the bank). Answer: **B**. The other sentences are about money.

(c) *Unreliable* = un + reliable, 'not able to be relied on'. The clue 'often arrived an hour late' supports this. Answer: **D**.

items_markdown: The meaning of a word depends on its sentence: look for definition, restatement, contrast, example and cause-and-effect clues.
Predict a meaning first, then use the substitution test: the chosen word must fit the sense and the grammar.
Prefixes and suffixes help: un-, dis-, in- and im- mean 'not'; -less means 'without'; re- means 'again'.
Read an idiom as a whole and think of the situation; never translate it word by word.
In the listening part, remember the sentence in which you heard the word and use the same clues.
